sources.title: Unhealthy air days drop nearly 75% from last year: EPA
Taichung Power upgrades to reduce its emissions

facts.text: PM2.5 means tiny particles floating in the air that are 2.5 micrometers across or smaller; it is measured in micrograms per cubic meter.
Fine particles in the air are linked to heart disease, lung disease and cancers.
Yearly average PM2.5 at the Zhongshan station in Taipei fell from 18.97 in 2015 to 12.53 in 2025 (micrograms per cubic meter).
Yearly average PM2.5 at the Zhongming station in Taichung fell from 24.87 in 2015 to 13.57 in 2025, a drop of 11.30.
Yearly average PM2.5 at the Qianjin station in Kaohsiung fell from 25.77 in 2015 to 16.09 in 2025, a drop of 9.68.
In 2015, the Kaohsiung station had the highest yearly average of the three stations and the Taipei station the lowest.
Upgrades to four boiler units at the coal-fired Taichung Power Plant were finished in 2020; the premier said they would cut the plant's air pollution by 80 percent over the next five years.
Some state-run companies replaced coal-fired boilers with gas-fired ones, which the environmental agency said helped reduce pollution.
From January to November 2022, rewards offered by the government took 1.68 million high-polluting motorcycles off Taiwan's roads.
The environmental agency said the cleaner air in 2022 was partly due to more rain and less pollution from abroad; pollution blown over from China fell by 20 to 30 percent that year.
A four-year government program aimed to bring the yearly PM2.5 average below 15 micrograms per cubic meter, and the agency judged it a success.
The agency said local pollution control cut pollutants by 82 percent, well beyond its 60 percent target.
Particulate matter in the air is commonly used as a measure of air pollution.
